primitives.name: Stroke Classification Accuracy
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Method Task protocol design (the paper's contribution): subtask 1 = global + per-class accuracy on trimmed clips; subtask 2 = COCO-style temporal mAP (20 IoU thresholds 0.5–0.95, step 0.05; detection = True when temporal IoU ≥ threshold) for ranking + frame-wise temporal IoU as secondary.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'total number of trimmed clips', 'y_i': 'true stroke class label', '\\hat{y}_i': 'predicted stroke class label', '\\mathbb{I}(\\cdot)': 'indicator function'}
primitives.assumptions: Each trimmed clip contains exactly one stroke or none; labels are mutually exclusive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When trimmed clips contain multiple strokes or ambiguous labeling.

layer2.mapping: Classification accuracy mirrors GSI's probabilistic label assignment with confidence thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Per-class and global accuracy scores from trimmed video clips.

primitives.name: Temporal Detection mAP
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Method Task protocol design (the paper's contribution): subtask 1 = global + per-class accuracy on trimmed clips; subtask 2 = COCO-style temporal mAP (20 IoU thresholds 0.5–0.95, step 0.05; detection = True when temporal IoU ≥ threshold) for ranking + frame-wise temporal IoU as secondary.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'IoU threshold ranging from 0.50 to 0.95', '\\text{AP}(t)': 'Average Precision at threshold t', '\\text{mAP}': 'mean Average Precision over IoU thresholds'}
primitives.assumptions: Temporal boundaries are well-defined; IoU thresholds are uniformly spaced.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When stroke boundaries are poorly defined or overlapping.

layer2.mapping: Temporal mAP is derived from frame-wise IoU and used in GSE for action boundary refinement.
layer2.telemetry: Mean average precision across 20 IoU thresholds for temporal stroke detection.

primitives.name: Frame-Wise IoU
primitives.verbatim_quote: Frame-wise IoU = overlap of predicted vs GT stroke frames across all videos.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'set of predicted stroke frames', 'G': 'set of ground truth stroke frames', '\\text{IoU}_{\\text{frame}}': 'intersection over union at frame level'}
primitives.assumptions: Predicted and ground truth stroke frames are binary indicators over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When frame-level predictions are sparse or misaligned temporally.

layer2.mapping: Frame-wise IoU acts as a secondary metric in GSE to validate temporal alignment.
layer2.telemetry: Average IoU score across all frames in detection task.

reasoning_traces.think:
The benchmark defines two core tasks: stroke classification and detection. Classification uses global and per-class accuracy, which aligns with GSI’s Bayesian label inference framework where each clip is treated as an independent observation. Detection employs COCO-style temporal mAP, a generalization of object detection metrics to temporal segments, enabling GSE to model action boundaries as time-series events. Frame-wise IoU provides a granular measure of alignment between predicted and actual stroke frames, useful for retroactive validation. The dual nature of these primitives—classification and temporal localization—reflects a fundamental duality in sports analytics: discrete event identification versus continuous motion tracking. Failure modes include misalignment of stroke boundaries, label ambiguity in trimmed clips, and poor temporal resolution in detection. These primitives form a layered abstraction where GSI handles probabilistic label assignment and GSE manages dynamic state transitions based on temporal IoU.
